source.title: Distribution of irreducible polynomials of small degrees over finite fields

accepted.question_text: Given a finite field F_q of order q, an element a in F_q, an integer n >= 2, and an integer j with 0 <= j < n, determine whether there exists a monic irreducible polynomial f(x) = x^n + sum_{k=0}^{n-1} a_k x^k over F_q whose j-th coefficient a_j is exactly a, except in the two exceptional cases: j = 0 and a = 0 for arbitrary q; and q = 2^m, n = 2, j = 1, and a = 0. Equivalently, is Hansen-Mullen Conjecture B true for all parameter choices outside these exceptions?

evidence.quote: Then there exists an irreducible polynomial f(x) = xn +Pn−1 k=0 akxk over Fq with aj = a except when
Conjecture B is indeed true in general.
